MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Fleetwood Mac and Eddie & The Cruisers fit the nostalgic rock mood reflected in my classic rock collections and The Cars listening.",
    "Carpenters Gold and The Ultimate Petula Clark connect with the melodic older vocal pop I enjoyed through Simon & Garfunkel and AM Gold; their collections also fit my repeated interest in hits."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Gershwin and Henry Mancini offer older music, but age alone is not the connection I want: today I prefer vocal pop and rock songs over orchestral or instrumental selections.",
    "Norah Jones has a plausible connection to Cheek to Cheek, but that does not outweigh my current interest in older hits. Paul Davis also did not give me enough personal familiarity to choose it today.",
    "I passed on 25 and Play On because I could not confidently connect those titles to an artist or sound I wanted; that uncertainty is different from disliking the music."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "Older music and greatest-hits collections seemed to be treated as enough of a match, even when the vocal style or sound did not fit my mood.",
    "My interest in Cheek to Cheek seemed to carry too much weight when suggesting another jazz-related choice for a session where I wanted older pop and rock hits."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "The combination of familiar vocals, memorable melodies, and a nostalgic pop or rock sound matters more to me right now than a shared era alone.",
    "A hits collection appeals most when I already have a clear connection to its artist or sound; the collection format by itself does not make me want to try it."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations understood my interest in nostalgic hit collections, but sometimes missed the familiar vocal pop and rock sound that makes those collections appealing to me now."
}
